meta.name: Fermi Arena
meta.author: Achim Imboden (concept with Claude)
meta.status: concept + starter build (no-AI tier playable); style deferred
meta.one_liner: A gamified Fermi-estimation trainer where the player builds a typed solution tree on a whiteboard and a mostly deterministic judge scores it; a model only answers narrow fixed-choice questions.

design_principles.detail: Accuracy, math, units, precision, calibration, time and triangulation are plain code. No model touches a number.
Every model call is a fixed-option question returning a probability distribution (Jev-style typed classifier). Scores come from code applied to those answers.
No Likert/1–5 judgments anywhere. Research shows graded criteria drift ~1 level low and disagree across judges; binary checks agree far better.

design_principles.rule: Ground truth or no accuracy score
design_principles.detail: A problem only enters ranked play if its answer has a citable source or is derived deterministically from one.
Each problem stores 1..n reference trees. An unmatched but unit-consistent tree is not wrong; it is scored on structure-agnostic checks.
If a classifier's top option is below threshold, the item is marked 'unsicher' and excluded from the score rather than silently decided.
Single-page artifact, no backend, no config system. Everything here should be buildable in one sitting per phase.

prior_art.name: allenai/fermi (RealFP + SynthFP)
prior_art.what_it_is: 867 real Fermi problems (train/val/test) + 10,000 templated ones. Solutions stored as programs: Q-nodes (sub-questions), F-facts, A-answers, P: final operation (Mul/Div/Add/Sub/Pow/Min/Log/Fac). Units via pint.
caveats: No LICENSE file in repo at time of inspection – cite the paper, verify terms before redistributing data

prior_art.name: LLM for Complex Reasoning: Fermi Problems study
what_we_take: Finding: GPT-4 tops out ~0.5 fp_score – Fermi is hard even for models, so the model must not be the one producing reference answers

prior_art.name: FermiEval – LLMs are overconfident
what_we_take: Calibration tracking: nominal 99% intervals covered truth only ~65% → the overconfidence pattern we want to train out of players

prior_art.name: Estimathon (Jane Street)
what_we_take: Proven game mechanic: min/max intervals, missing intervals double your score, lowest score wins
Limited resubmissions as a tension mechanic

prior_art.name: CheckEval
what_we_take: Decompose soft judgments into binary checklist questions
+0.45 average inter-evaluator agreement vs Likert, lower variance

prior_art.name: Jev vs. LLMs as Rubric Judges
what_we_take: Typed classifier matched flash-tier LLM judges in 19/27 comparisons, better on binary criteria
Judges' errors are correlated → ensembles/cascades add little; validate against own human labels instead

prior_art.name: Proper scoring rule for confidence intervals
Commercial AI case coaches (e.g. casegrade.io, soreno.ai)
what_we_take: Gap check: they appear to use holistic LLM rubric grading; no typed-tree + deterministic judge found → our differentiator
prior_art.verified: Landing pages / roundup only, not product-tested

internal.name: Fermi Problems: Interview Strategy Research (Claude Doc)

phases.player_does: Reads the problem; archetype hidden in ranked mode
Picks/writes up to 2 clarifying assumptions (scope, unit, time frame)
Builds the tree on the whiteboard: factor cards + operations, no values yet
Fills value, unit, reason per leaf; optional low/high per leaf
Second path or benchmark; names weakest assumption; writes so-what
Sees scorecard, truth, per-slot feedback, badges

game_loop.timer_rule: Phases are soft – overtime is allowed but recorded and reduces the speed component only.

modes.description: Archetype visible, hints on, reference slots revealed after verdict.
One shared problem per day, full judge, streak counter.
Estimathon-style: 8 problems in 20 min, only min/max per problem, 3 resubmissions. Pure code scoring.
Phase 2: after verdict, interviewer pushes on the weakest slot; player revises one value and defends it. Judged by checklist only.

Dimension.description: Unit as exponent vector over base dimensions. Enables deterministic unit checking without a units library.

properties.to_base: number (factor to base unit, e.g. 'pro Woche' → time base day = 1/7)

properties.archetype: enum: recurring_consumption | durable_goods | service_supply | physical_capacity | single_site_revenue | b2b_market
properties.region: enum: CH | Basel | Zurich | EU | World
properties.accepted_clarifications: string[] (canonical scope assumptions, e.g. 'Stadt, nicht Agglomeration')
properties.benchmarks: Benchmark[] (known numbers a good sanity check could cite)

properties.derivation: string (only for status=derived: formula from verified inputs)

Slot.description: A named, expected factor in a reference tree. This is what player cards get mapped onto.

properties.aliases_de: string[] (helps the mapping classifier and allows exact-match shortcut)
properties.point_reference: number (centre value used for per-slot bias tracking)
properties.segmentable: bool (does splitting this slot into segments show insight?)

SolutionTree.description: Typed program, inspired by allenai/fermi. Nodes are either leaves (estimated factors) or operations.

properties.label: string (player's own words)
properties.slot_id: string | null (filled by mapping stage, never by player)

properties.op: enum: mul | div | add | sub | segment_sum

Attempt.description: Everything the player submits. The whiteboard is just an editor for this object.

properties.final_value: number (computed by code from tree – player cannot type it)

ClassifierQuestion.description: The ONLY interface to a model. Fixed options in, distribution out.

properties.options: string[] (closed set, always includes an escape option like 'keine' / 'unklar')
properties.threshold: number (min top-option probability to accept, default 0.7)

ClassifierQuestion.returns: { distribution: { option: probability }, top: option, accepted: bool }

properties.feedback_de: string[] (template sentences filled by code, not generated)

judge_pipeline.overview: Three layers. L1 and the aggregation are pure functions. L2/L3 call the classifier only for closed questions. The same Attempt always yields the same ScoreCard given the same classifier outputs (cache by hash).

checks: Every leaf has value, unit, reason
Final unit dimension equals problem.answer_unit dimension
stages.on_fail: Return to whiteboard with highlighted node; no score.

components.formula: 1 if dimension algebra of every op is valid (add/sub/segment_sum need equal dims), else 0
share of leaf values with ≤2 significant figures
1 − |Σ sign(round_dir_i)| / n_leaves, where round_dir compares value to nearest 'raw' input the player typed before rounding (only if raw captured)

components.note: Within ~1 order of magnitude counts; agreement within 2× ≈ 0.7

components.formula: Winkler: (U − L) + (2/α)·max(0, L − y, y − U), computed in log10 space, mapped to 0..1 vs problem-specific baseline

stages.engine: exact alias match first, classifier second
steps: For each player leaf: if label normalised ∈ slot.aliases_de of any reference tree → map deterministically.
Else ask Q_MAP_SLOT with options = all slot labels of the best-matching reference tree + 'keiner davon'.
Pick reference tree with maximum mapped-slot overlap (Jaccard). Ties → fewer unmapped leaves.

components.formula: |mapped required slots| / |required slots| of chosen tree
components.fallback: If best Jaccard < 0.3 → tree is 'eigener Ansatz': coverage = null (deferred), unit_consistency and triangulation carry structure weight

components.formula: mean over mapped leaves of: 1 if log10(value) ∈ slot.plausible_log10_range else max(0, 1 − distance_to_range / 1)
1 if a segment_sum node sits on a slot with segmentable=true, else 0
1 if weakest_slot_node_id set AND that node has the widest low/high log-span OR largest |log10 ratio| vs reference (code-checked, not model-checked)

stages.weights_rationale: Mirrors interviewer priorities: structure and assumptions above the final number (Hacking the Case Interview ranking). Accuracy deliberately ≤15%.
stages.null_handling: Deferred components are dropped and remaining weights renormalised; card shows 'unsicher' list.
stages.total: round(100 · Σ w_i · c_i / Σ w_i over non-null)

determinism_guarantees: Classifier outputs cached by sha256(question_id + normalised input); replays never re-call.
Temperature-free engine preferred (typed classifier). If an LLM is used as fallback: constrained to output exactly one option token; distribution approximated by 5 samples or logprobs.
Feedback text is template-filled by code from component values – no free generation in the verdict.
judge_pipeline.validation_plan: Hand-label 30 attempts; run all three tiers on the same attempts; report agreement (Cohen's κ) per question. Tells how much AI adds over pure code.

standout_signals.description: What separates good from excellent candidates (PrepLounge, Hacking the Case Interview, LessWrong) – each made checkable and turned into a badge.

badges.signal: Solves top-down and bottom-up, paths agree
Splits population where one average would lie
Checks against a benchmark and lands close
Names the assumption most likely wrong – and it really is

badges.rule: Over last 20 interval answers at 90%: hit rate 80–95%

badges.signal: Translates the number into a decision
Recognises and executes a question type reliably

pattern_learning.description: Typed data makes personal patterns measurable instead of 'felt'.

metrics.formula: per slot: running mean of log10(player_value / slot.point_reference)
per confidence level: hits / n where truth ∈ [low, high]
metrics.feedback_template_de: Deine 90%-Intervalle treffen nur {rate}% – mach sie breiter.

metrics.formula: Elo vs problem difficulty: expected = 1/(1+10^((D−R)/400)), D = 800 + 150·difficulty, outcome = total/100, K = 32
median seconds per phase over last 10
metrics.feedback_template_de: Du springst nach {s}s in die Zahlen – nimm dir 60s für die Struktur.

metrics.formula: counts of: unit_consistency=0, precision_hygiene<0.5, sanity_check=0, clarification=0

progression.xp: xp = total (0..100) + 10 per badge + 5 streak bonus
progression.streak: Daily mode attempt submitted on consecutive calendar days (local time).

how_this_was_built.summary: Concept assembled in one Cowork session on 2026-10-01 from web research, one cloned repository and the preceding strategy doc.
steps: Researched interview Fermi strategy (Hacking the Case Interview, IGotAnOffer, LessWrong, The Aperiodical) → Claude Doc 'Fermi Problems: Interview Strategy Research'.
Searched for prior art on Fermi datasets, scoring and LLM judging; read FermiEval, the 2025 Fermi LLM study, CheckEval and the Jev-vs-LLM judge paper.

Cloned github.com/allenai/fermi and inspected record format (question/program/answer/context), the eval_utils accuracy metric and dataset sizes (realFP 867 across splits as shipped; README says 928). Noted missing LICENSE file.
Checked Estimathon rules on estimathon.com for the interval mechanic.
Derived the design: computable components in code, soft judgments as fixed-option classifier questions, Likert removed, truth gating, multi-tree references.
Wrote schemas, pipeline formulas, classifier catalog, badges, pattern metrics, two sample problems (one ranked via derived truth, one marked to_verify).
v0.2: added three tiers on one interface; built the starter repo (ES modules, no deps), wrote 10 tests, built the single-file version and ran the tutorial loop headless in Chromium.
not_verified: Commercial tools' internal scoring (only marketing pages/roundup)
Jev API availability and pricing for this project
Weights in L4 are a reasoned starting point, not empirically fitted

tiers.principle: One judge, three ways to answer the five closed questions. Numbers are always scored by code. Ratings are kept separately per tier.

noai.how: Every closed question becomes a constrained player input; nothing is classified.

inputs.Q_MAP_SLOT: Player tags each leaf with a reference slot – list revealed only in the 'Prüfen' phase, after the tree is built with own labels
inputs.Q_CLARIFY: Chips Umfang/Einheit/Zeitraum, each counts only with text ≥ 5 chars
inputs.Q_BENCHMARK: Pick a benchmark from the problem + note ≥ 10 chars, or build a second path
inputs.Q_SO_WHAT: Sentence frame 'Das heisst: ___, weil ___', both blanks ≥ 10 chars

noai.known_weakness: Self-tagging is gameable and recognition is easier than recall – acceptable for solo training; ranked separately.

local.how: Qwen (or any Ollama model) answers the closed questions via structured output: JSON schema with enum of allowed options, temperature 0.
local.status: implemented, untested against a live Ollama
requirements: Ollama running with OLLAMA_ORIGINS=* (or the page's origin)
Browser may block https→http://localhost (Private Network Access) – run the local build via 'npm run dev' if so

frontier.how: Anthropic Messages API from the browser (anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access header), forced to answer JSON with one option; parsed and validated against the option list.
frontier.status: implemented, untested; personal-use only (key in localStorage)
later: Jev typed classifier as alternative engine if API access exists

tiers.comparison_study: Hand-label 30 attempts; run all three tiers on the same attempts; report agreement (Cohen's κ) per question. Tells how much AI adds over pure code.

simplifications_vs_concept: Reference trees are stored as slot sets + a display formula, not full typed trees – coverage only needs the set
Interval is entered once for the final answer (90%), not per leaf
Calibration is shown and tracked but not part of the weighted total (badge 'Kalibriert' instead)
Unit errors don't block submission; they score unit_consistency = 0 and accuracy = 0
Classifier distribution approximated by a single temperature-0 answer; no threshold yet
tested: 10 node tests (fpScore matches allenai accuracy_metric, Winkler, units, determinism, deferral, weakest-assumption check, profile)
Headless browser run of the full tutorial loop on the built single file: score 90, no console errors
